- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes.
- Model overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices show strong upward momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: forecasts tend to revert to lower levels after recent high prices, but true prices often continue trending upward.
- Model lags behind true price movements by 2–5 days, especially in upward trends — forecasts are too early to capture the peak.
- When true prices spike sharply, model forecasts overshoot the peak and then fail to correct, leading to overcorrection in later days.
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 10 days — true prices often show stronger upward momentum than forecasted.
- Model tends to smooth out short-term volatility, leading to underestimation of price swings in the middle of the forecast horizon.
- Model shows persistent bias toward lower values in the first 10 days, especially when historical prices are trending upward.
